skill.name: contacts-at-target-accounts
skill.description: Find and rank business contacts at companies you already target using Leadsets. Optionally enrich selected contacts with current roles and work email verification statuses.
skill.summary: Rank contacts at target accounts and optionally enrich them with Leadsets.
skill.author: leadsets

security_audit.summary: Twenty-two alerts are Markdown, documentation, or output-field false positives; the Leadsets connection does send target domains and search filters to an external service. Two separate risks remain: contact exports lack a sharing check, and the enrichment instructions conflict on which emails are verified. No evidence of shell execution, host reconnaissance, credential exfiltration, or prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: Account domains and search filters are sent to Leadsets.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose which fields Leadsets receives and require authorization before sending confidential account lists. Keep input limited to domains and necessary role filters.

remediation.issue: Contact exports do not require a destination sharing check.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the exact external destination and its intended audience before writing. Omit work email fields if access cannot be verified.

remediation.issue: Enrichment instructions conflict on whether every returned email is verified.
remediation.suggestion: Use the returned status as the sole verification source. Remove blanket verification claims and test that catch-all, unknown, and missing addresses stay outside the verified segment.

semantic_findings.title: Contact exports lack a destination sharing check
semantic_findings.description: The workflow writes names and optional work emails to a selected sheet or CRM. It does not check whether everyone with access is authorized to see those fields.

semantic_findings.description: The rules require verified status, but the enrichment step says returned emails are already verified. An agent could ignore the returned status and mislabel unconfirmed addresses.

content.value_statement: An account list tells you which companies to target, but not whom to contact. Use Leadsets to rank people at each account and optionally check their current roles and work emails.
actual_capabilities: Normalizes company domains, removes duplicates, and lists accounts without usable domains.
Converts role descriptions into title, function, and seniority filters and tests them on the first account.
Checks Leadsets usage limits and estimates search and enrichment records before a full run.
Ranks contacts per account by seniority, title fit, and match reasons, then removes duplicate people.
Optionally enriches selected contacts, records work email statuses, and flags contacts who have moved companies.
Reports contacts and unmatched accounts in CSV, or writes to a selected sheet or CRM through an existing connection.
limitations: Requires a Leadsets account and either a configured MCP connection or a REST API key.
Does not discover new accounts or guess missing domains or email addresses.
Keeps up to ten contacts per account and may pause when Leadsets usage or rate limits are reached.
Does not send outreach or create CRM records on its own.

use_cases.title: Prioritize contacts for named accounts
use_cases.description: Find and rank revenue leaders at a list of assigned domains before deciding whom to contact.

use_cases.title: Map potential buyers
use_cases.description: Find operations directors at a list of prospective customer companies without requesting work emails.

use_cases.title: Review contact coverage
use_cases.description: Review which accounts have matching people, which lack usable domains, and which need further research.

prompt_templates.title: Find contacts at two accounts
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: a short list with default filters.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find contacts at [domain A] and [domain B] using the default filters. Leave enrichment off and return a CSV.

prompt_templates.title: Search for a specific role
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: explicit role and seniority requirements.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find two revenue operations leaders at director level or above for each domain in [account list]. Include match reasons and accounts with no matches.

prompt_templates.title: Enrich selected contacts
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: shortlist enrichment and email status review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Rank three sales leaders per account in [account list] and enrich only the selected contacts. Separate email statuses and flag people who changed companies.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a batch and export results
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: a larger run with a connected destination.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check Leadsets usage before searching [account list] for revenue leaders. Confirm the destination and its sharing settings before writing to [sheet]. Report records used and what remains.

output_examples.input: Find two sales leaders per domain in a three-account list. Leave enrichment off.
output: Two accounts searched; one account was set aside because it had no domain.
One account returned two ranked contacts; the other had no matches.
The CSV lists each contact's title and match reasons. Email columns are omitted.

output_examples.input: Find and enrich three revenue operations leaders per account for four domains.
output: Four accounts searched; three had matches and one had none.
Seven contacts kept: four verified work emails, one catch-all, one unknown, and one with no email.
One contact was flagged because enrichment returned a different current company.

best_practices: Provide company domains and clear role criteria to reduce mismatches.
Review the first search result and the usage estimate before continuing with a large list.
Enable enrichment only when needed, and confirm who can access a shared destination before exporting work emails.
anti_patterns: Using the skill to discover companies instead of providing a target account list.
Treating a catch-all address, unknown address, or old CRM email as verified.
Exporting work emails to a shared sheet or CRM without checking access.

faq.question: What input do I need?
faq.answer: Provide company domains as pasted text or through an accessible CSV, sheet, or CRM view. The skill flags names without domains.

faq.question: What filters does the skill use by default?
faq.answer: It searches for revenue roles at VP or head level and keeps up to three contacts per account.

faq.question: Do I need a Leadsets connection?
faq.answer: Yes. Use a configured Leadsets MCP connection or a Leadsets REST API key.

faq.question: Are work emails included automatically?
faq.answer: No. Enrichment is off by default, and only addresses with a returned verified status should be treated as verified.

faq.question: Where can I receive results?
faq.answer: CSV is the default. A selected Google Sheet or CRM destination requires an existing connection with write access.

faq.question: What happens if I reach a usage limit?
faq.answer: The workflow can pause, report completed work, and identify where to resume. Available records depend on your Leadsets plan.
